In conditional expressions, the `Decidable` instance for the proposition is used to select a branch. At run time, this case distinction code is identical to that which would be generated for a `Bool`-based conditional. In proofs, the tactic `decide` synthesizes an instance of `Decidable p`, attempts to reduce `decide p` to `true`, and then succeeds with the proof `of_decide_eq_true rfl` if it can. Because `Decidable` carries data, when writing `@[simp]` lemmas which include a `Decidable` instance on the LHS, it is best to use `{_ : Decidable p}` rather than `[Decidable p]` so that non-canonical instances can be found via unification rather than instance synthesis.
